messages:
emma_oncall: Heads-up — customer reported p99 jump after yesterday's routing rollout. Support logs show p99 ~1.2s for /v1/generate, but our APM traces for the same timeframe show ~580ms. Grafana panel (service:frontend, quantile:0.99) matches the 1.2s. Any ideas on where the extra 600ms is coming from? @tara_obs @kai_sre

tara_obs: Can you paste the support sample + trace ids? my first guess is mismatched quantile sources (ingest vs downstream rollups) or different tag filtering on the dashboard.

emma_oncall: Support sample: trace ids `trc-48a2` and `trc-48b3`. Customer timeframe: 2026-03-16T22:10-22:25 UTC. They say it started right after the route-policy v3 canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: route-policy v3 -> canary 80% at 2026-03-16T22:14 UTC by jason_platform. No service restarts.

kai_sre: Quick sanity: APM traces measure end-to-end (client->frontend->backend). Grafana panel probably reads pre-rollup times from metrics ingest (agent-side). If we applied a sampling or aggregation change in the ingest pipeline with the rollout, quantiles can diverge.

jason_platform: We changed routing for cold-prefixes to add a fallback path (adds a hop to a routing proxy) in v3 for ~10% of requests. That could add latency on tails if fallback rate spiked. But the rollout was only 80% to be clear (so more requests got v3). No change to metric tags.

tara_obs: I queried the raw histogram buckets from the metrics store for that timeframe. Quick diff: pre-rollout p99 (raw buckets) ~610ms, post-rollout raw buckets p99 ~1.18s. But APM traces show p99 570ms -> 610ms. So traces don't show the tail. That suggests the metric ingestion path is inflating some counts into >1s bucket. Could be duplicated events or delayed aggregated events.

infra-bot: Notice: metric-ingest pipeline had a retry storm at 22:16 UTC for 3m due to transient Thrift timeouts; backlog replays queued and were processed later with higher latency metadata.

kai_sre: Bingo — backlog replay can surface as large-latency samples (ingest time) if we tag latency using ingest timestamp instead of event timestamp. If Grafana panel uses ingest-time derived buckets and APM uses event-time, they won't match.

emma_oncall: Support wants mitigation and repro steps to explain to customer. Short term: can we 1) filter the panel to event_time (if possible) or 2) exclude the 22:16-22:19 window where ingest retries happened?

tara_obs: I can change the Grafana panel to use the event_time metric dimension (if available) and hide backlog-processed samples. If we don't have event_time, add a dashboard annotation and filter `ingest_retry = true` to exclude.

jason_platform: For mitigation: rolling back v3 is an option but I don't think it's root cause now. Plan: 1) tara update dashboard; 2) infra to confirm replay origin + mark those samples; 3) send customer a clear timeline explaining retry/replay.

emma_oncall: Agreed. I'll draft the customer note once infra confirms. Thanks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Replay source: agent batch retry queue drained at 22:18:40 UTC — reason: transient thrift timeout to collector (resolved). Marked metrics with `ingest_retry=true`.

kai_sre: Followup: add a monitoring alert if ingest_retry rate spikes >0 for >1m so we don't mix replayed records into production quantiles. Filed issue INFRA-1298.

emma_oncall: Filed support note draft in #support-drafts, will ping for review. Closing loop here for eng-oncall.
